html:
SMTO-POL-0031 — This permission request covers too many items

GUID: 28eb9117-5502-5e0e-8993-f52eb36d378e
Slug: resource-request-limit
Domain: POL · Subsystem: resource-access

What happened

  • Some items are on computers SMTO also needs your permission to use. Adding those computers made the question bigger than 16 items, so it wasn't shown and no access was given.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send a message asking SMTO to ask for permission in smaller groups, for example only the items on one computer at a time. Each item on a computer not yet chosen for this task also adds that computer to the question.
  2. For a new request, open the target menu (headed Execution target) in the message area and select the Gateways the work needs before you send it. Gateways (the computers SMTO works on) that are already selected don't need to be added to the permission question.
  3. Keep the selection to 16 Gateways or fewer. SMTO allows at most 16 Gateways in one task and 16 items in one permission question.

What success looks like

  • A permission card appears listing the items and their computers, and SMTO continues after you answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't allow access to a computer you didn't mean to include; approving an item never quietly allows the computer it lives on.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • request_resource_access was rejected because adding the host Gateway resources that the requested items require pushed the request above sixteen resources.

What this means

  • A discovered resource can require explicit authority for its host Gateway. The controller adds missing Gateway resources before freezing the question, then rejects an expanded set larger than sixteen. The initially supplied reference count can therefore fit while the complete request does not.

Why this can happen

  • A discovered resource can require explicit authority for its host Gateway. The controller adds missing Gateway resources before freezing the question, then rejects an expanded set larger than sixteen. The initially supplied reference count can therefore fit while the complete request does not.

How to diagnose it

  • Count the explicit resources together with distinct host Gateway resources that are not already authorized.

How to fix it

  • Request fewer resources so the items plus any Gateway resources not already in the task's base or user-selected Gateways or covered by an active Gateway grant total sixteen or fewer. Selecting the hosting Gateways for the task before submitting avoids adding them to the request; never drop required host authority.
  • Request a smaller resource set that leaves room for each required Gateway permission.

Retry and execution caution

  • Retry a smaller permission request; do not replay resource operations.

How to verify the fix

  • The expanded request fits within sixteen resources and displays one bounded permission question.

What not to do

  • Do not omit required host authority or treat a resource request as an implicit grant to its machine.

Technical notes

  • The oversized question is not published and no grant is committed.
  • The rejection does not identify which resources the user would approve.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
